summary: This Restaurant class holds a single method, getSpiceLevel, that turns a number from 1 to 5 into a readable spice description like "Mild" or "Spicy". It is a small, testable unit: give it a number, get a string back.

lines.text: The method takes one int and hands back a String, which is exactly the shape that makes testing easy — a test passes in a level and compares the returned text to what it expects.
This is a switch expression, not a switch statement: the whole switch produces a value, and that value is what gets returned. Notice there are no break statements, so no accidental fall-through.
The arrow form pairs each level with its description in one line. Each case here matches a single value and yields the string for it.

Every switch expression needs a branch that always matches, since it must produce a value; default catches 0, 6, negatives, and anything else outside the menu. Note that this version reports the problem as text rather than throwing an exception — a worthwhile test case either way.
